transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-05-20 14:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Mark Reyes (CopperGate - Head of ML), Anya Patel (CopperGate - Security Manager), Liam O'Connor (CopperGate - Platform)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be rough): quick checkin on SSO flakiness from last week, demo of audit log export, discussion on retention and SOC two evidence, agreed action items.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey team thanks for joining, should we do a quick round of who’s on the call, then jump into the SSO errors and the log export?
[00:08] Mark Reyes: yep mark here, give the quick context we spun up the POC in our sandbox, seeing intermittent 401s when sessions are > 20 minutes so want to get SSO stable before we push to staging
[00:18] Anya Patel: Anya here, primarily interested in audit trail - we need to show tamper evidence for SOC 2 and also a retention policy that's legal.
[00:28] Priya Kapoor: priya from redwood, i'll take the lead on the SSO debug, looks like a session-cookie vs token expiry mismatch in your idp assertion, maybe a clock skew but we'll validate
[00:40] Liam O'Connor: liam - platform, we also need to understand what logs look like when requests hit the dediate pool, sorry i mean dedicated pool, redwood ded- uh the dedicated nodes, we want to map them into our splunk pipeline
[00:54] Jordan Lee: great, ok first SSO - we ran the reproducer last night and saw two classes of failures: 1) expired assertion on long-running chats, 2) race on session refresh where the client retries before the idp issues new token.
[01:12] Mark Reyes: yeah that matches, for long chains we're seeing the assistant requesting new tokens and the idp returning an old audience claim, maybe metadata mismatch
[01:22] Priya Kapoor: i'm thinking we add a guard in our middleware to request token refresh proactively at t minus 60 seconds to avoid the race, that should be a low-risk shim. we'll share patch in jira.
[01:34] Anya Patel: quick question - how does that affect audit logs? like will we get a consistent trace id across refreshes? we need to link events for SOC 2 traceability.
[01:44] Priya Kapoor: yes, good call - our runtime emits a request_id for each conversation turn and that persists across token refreshes. note though in Dedicated we currently attach node_id and pool_id and sometimes the field names were changed in the last run — there was a small schema drift (we call it KV cash in older exports, ha)
[02:00] Liam O'Connor: haha KV cash, noted. can you share a sample log so we can map fields into splunk? format preference is JSON lines with ISO timestamps and a correlation_id.
[02:12] Jordan Lee: yes we'll push a sanitized sample. Priya, you have the export from yesterday?
[02:18] Priya Kapoor: i do, i'll drop a redacted ndjson to the shared drive after this call. it will include request_id, convo_id, node_id, model_variant, event_type, timestamp. watch out - sometimes model_variant shows internal names like rwd-7b-q8 which may be sensitive for them, we'll obfuscate.
[02:36] Mark Reyes: perfect. on retention, our legal team requires 13 months for logs and 7 years for admin audit trails, is that something Redwood can support on hosted? or do we need Private?
[02:48] Jordan Lee: hosted defaults are 90 days for raw token-level logs, but we have archive options to push to S3 for longer retention. For encrypted long-term retention with customer KMS, that's only available on Private (VPC) deployments today — or via a dedicated contract for hosted that adds KMS integration.
[03:06] Anya Patel: so for SOC two we need proof of immutability and key ownership, i guess that speaks to KMS/HSM. can you outline the difference quickly?
[03:16] Priya Kapoor: sure — hosted with Redwood-managed keys means we control the encryption keys but we provide audit logs and key rotation records. Private with customer-managed KMS gives you explicit key control and HSM-backed keys if you need them, and the logs are stored in your VPC or on-prem store so legal team is happier.
[03:30] Liam O'Connor: do you support bringing your own HSM? like an external HSM that we run?
[03:36] Jordan Lee: yes, for private we integrate with customer KMS and HSM — we have a few partners integrated. i'll follow up with the integration matrix.
[03:44] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[03:46] Anya Patel: Another SOC2 item - we need proof of RBAC controls around who can unredact logs, who can access raw transcripts. How granular is Redwood's RBAC?
[03:56] Priya Kapoor: we support role-based policies with per-route tokens; the console supports RBAC roles for viewer/editor/audit. there's also token scoping so you can create tokens that only allow embeddings or only allow read-only access to evals. We'll also show audit logs of console actions.
[04:14] Mark Reyes: that's good. can the audit logs show the exact query text? sometimes we need to redact PII but still show that an action occurred.
[04:24] Priya Kapoor: logs include a hashed payload field for content (sha256) and a reference id so you can verify existence without storing plaintext. For customers who need plaintext for e-discovery we offer an encrypted archive option under private where keys are customer-managed.
[04:40] Jordan Lee: ok next i want to walk through the sample export priya will paste. but before that, any blockers from coppergate side?
[04:48] Liam O'Connor: network-wise we need to confirm egress rules for the private agent if we go that route — ports, outbound ranges. I'll coordinate with infra.
[04:56] Anya Patel: also need a compliance contact for SOC 2 pre-audit questions — that'll be Karen from legal but i'll loop her in after this call.
[05:06] Jordan Lee: perfect. Priya, can you share the sample log now?
[05:10] Priya Kapoor: sure i will paste a short snippet, text only, redacted.
[05:14] [05:14] Priya Kapoor: {"timestamp":"2026-05-19T22:44:12Z","request_id":"req-8a4f","convo_id":"conv-11","node_id":"ded-3","event_type":"token_refresh","model_variant":"rwd-7b-q8","payload_hash":"<redacted>"}
[05:42] Mark Reyes: thanks, that lines up. can you add user_id or user_role? we need to tie events to internal user ids for audit.
[05:50] Priya Kapoor: yes we can add an actor_id field. note privacy wise we recommend pseudonymization if you need to retain user textual content beyond 90 days.
[06:02] Anya Patel: that's fine, we will pseudonymize. about retention pipeline, what's the recommended approach for exporting to our S3 with lifecycle rules?
[06:12] Jordan Lee: two options — push raw logs to a tenant bucket on hosted with lifecycle, or use the Private deployment where logs never leave your VPC. For our hosted push we can set up a delivery agent that exports daily ndjson to your S3. retention/lifecycle then becomes your responsibility.
[06:26] Liam O'Connor: for the POC we prefer the pushed-to-S3 route so we can try retention policy without full private install. what's the SLA on that agent?
[06:34] Priya Kapoor: daily export is reliable; near-real-time streaming is available as part of our premium logging add-on. for POC daily is fine. we'll put the connector in place for dev bucket.
[06:44] Mark Reyes: ok makes sense. next on the agenda: evidence for SOC two. Anya, can you remind us what CopperGate's scope is?
[06:52] Anya Patel: we're scoping infra and platform, specifically anything that processes customer data in the POC. we need to surface: access logs, change control, incident logs, and who has admin console access.
[07:04] Jordan Lee: we can produce console admin audit trails and change history for model config changes and rollout events. for incident logs we pull alert traces and timestamps. For change control we can provide PR-level traceback if changes happened through our infra.
[07:18] Anya Patel: will those artifacts have signed timestamps or some integrity proof?
[07:24] Priya Kapoor: we append a signature field where possible and maintain a chain-of-custody record for key artifacts. For hosted it's a Redwood-signed record; for private you can sign with your own KMS keys.
[07:38] Mark Reyes: good. a couple of smaller things we hit during testing: thread context is lost sometimes after we hit certain token sizes, and that affects trace linkage. is that a logging bug or model behaviour?
[07:50] Priya Kapoor: likely a runtime truncation at the kv cache boundary — we've seen race conditions where the cache key was different due to whitespace normalization. we'll instrument additional trace points to capture the convo context hash.
[08:04] Jordan Lee: i'll add that to the ticket backlog and push a low-risk fix to staging; not expected to affect PII handling but will help correlation for audit.
[08:14] Anya Patel: excellent. for the SSO test, Mark and I will run the test matrix and share failing saml responses; we'll also include idp metadata.
[08:24] Mark Reyes: yes we'll send two failing SAML assertions and one successful assertion case.
[08:30] Jordan Lee: perfect. we'll also add a proactive refresh shim as discussed, and Priya will validate request_id continuity so you can link events.
[08:40] Priya Kapoor: quick note on RBAC - we can create an "auditor" role with read-only access to logs and restricted access to raw transcripts; that role's actions are also logged.
[08:52] Liam O'Connor: can that auditor role be restricted to specific environments? we don't want auditors hitting prod but only POC/staging.
[08:58] Priya Kapoor: yes scoping by environment is supported via route-level permissions.
[09:04] Jordan Lee: ok let's capture the concrete deliverables. Jordan to send SSO checklist and sample shim; Priya to post sanitized ndjson; Anya to provide SOC2 contacts and retention windows; Liam to confirm egress rules.
[09:18] Anya Patel: timeline wise, our compliance pre-check is scheduled for 2026-06-02 - we'd like to have the artifacts in by 2026-05-28.
[09:28] Jordan Lee: noted, we'll target the 5/25-5/26 window for all artifacts.
[09:34] Mark Reyes: one last Q - do you have a quick note on competitor behaviors? we tested a small setup with another vendor and they didn't have persistent request_ids which made correlation impossible, so it's good you provide that out of the box.
[09:48] Jordan Lee: appreciate that, we try to bake in traceability. any other open items?
[09:54] Liam O'Connor: none from me.
[09:56] Mark Reyes: all good.
[09:58] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, i'll send the follow-ups. meeting adjourned.

Call end.
